comments.body: I would submit a screenshot of your full character reference, generate some references for clothing and armor, and have a site make you the 3D model for it. Or, you can generate a reference with your character in the clothing/armor you want, and just retexture your existing character

comments.author: ongix
comments.body:
Hopefully this helps you but from my experience there are a few ways to do it with AI:

2D concept w/ your favorite LLM and then either:

1. Meshy/Trippo/Hunyuan etc. to generate and paint a 3D out of. Usually the problem you'll face here is dimensions not being correct. You can use Blender to tweak those for yourself or even ask opus/sol. For stuff with joints (shirt/pants) I recommend asking opus/sol to rig it first with the same skeleton as your model and then aligning it with that, really helps IMO.
2. Blender MCP + Opus/Sol. Take the torso for example and ask them implement the 2D concept out of. This means they take the torso, scale it up a bit and start modifying & generating textures and applying.

Either way make sure you validate what they do in Blender because they do tend to sometimes miss a spot or not follow directions at some point. And also I recommend you work part by part. So do not generate the entire full-body armor. Generate the shirt, the pants, the gloves, the shoes, etc. This will really help your AI nail that specific part and also if you use 2D->3D generation (1) it can save you from stuff that just can not fit without scaling or mangling them.
